findings.criterion: 1 — resident can generate and share a usable, tamper-protected 2-hour pass
findings.issue: The joined test still starts from a fabricated token, mounts GuestPass directly, and mocks lookup/redeem success. It does not execute resident generation/share, the real /pass route through AppProvider, or server HMAC, verify-code, version, and expiry validation for the QR it displays.
findings.consequence: There is still no in-context proof that the artifact a resident actually sends survives unauthenticated bootstrap and is accepted by the real gate as that same live two-hour pass.
findings.correction: Issue a live pass through the API, invoke the real resident Share control, open its fragment URL through /pass at a mobile viewport, decode the rendered QR, and perform real lookup/redeem; assert exact token identity, two-hour expiry, and HMAC plus verify-code tamper rejection.

findings.criterion: 3 and 4 — camera plate scanning during check-in and check-out
findings.issue: The rendered tests replace LiveCamera with a button that emits an already-decoded plate, so getUserMedia, the shipped ONNX/model loader and decoder, a camera fixture, and a responsive browser remain unexecuted. The existing fake-camera browser story has no recorded run and covers check-in only.
findings.consequence: Actual camera acquisition and plate decoding in the shipped stack remain unverified for both attendant flows.
findings.correction: Run and record the 390x844 fake-camera check-in story with the real model and .y4m fixture, add and run the equivalent checkout story, and assert the visible plate, checkout match request/result, browser/model/fixture versions, and clean console.

findings.criterion: 6 and 7 — complete Admin CRUD and Super Admin cross-property operations
findings.issue: The rendered CRUD test still performs create/edit/delete only for a unit. People is used only to switch a selector and observe a units read; Parking is never mounted, no person/site/slot mutation is driven, no write is performed in the second property, no API denial is executed for a regular admin, and no narrow viewport is used.
findings.consequence: Required person/building/slot UI CRUD, mobile usability, Super Admin writes across properties, and the regular-admin property boundary remain unverified in context.
findings.correction: Drive create/edit/delete for person, site, unit, and slot through the real screens at a narrow viewport; switch a Super Admin to a second property and perform representative writes there; execute regular-admin cross-property read/write denials against the API.

findings.criterion: cross-cutting security/data integrity — idempotency on required CRUD writes
findings.issue: replaySafe correctly replays an explicitly repeated key, but each real post() invocation defaults to a fresh random key and the forms retain no submission key across a lost response or double submit. A user retry therefore does not hit the stored response and still reaches unit_exists/site_exists/etc. POST /v1/users and POST /v1/platform/tenants/:slug/members are not replaySafe/idempotent at all, so their client-sent keys are ignored; after local-auth person creation commits, loss of the first response strands the one-time password and retry reaches already_member. The new API test manually reuses one key and does not exercise either real client retry or person creation.
findings.consequence: Ordinary retry/double-tap paths can still report failure after successful CRUD, duplicate side effects/audits, and leave a newly created person without a recoverable credential.
findings.correction: Keep a submission-scoped key in each CRUD form and reuse it until that payload succeeds or is deliberately changed, with pending controls preventing double submit. Require or honor that key on tenant and platform person creation too, but replace raw one-time-password replay with an invitation/password-setup or explicit credential-recovery flow. Add lost-response UI retry tests and same-key unit/site/slot/person API tests proving one mutation/audit and a usable person-onboarding outcome.
